grade.primary_choice: Keep Laravel; cache public reads at a CDN and on the server, slim down per-user endpoints, add temporary capacity, load test
red_flags_hit: Leaving the default rate limiter in place (it never looks at Laravel's default throttle and suggests per-IP limits without considering mobile carrier NAT)
unsupported_claims: 'A few hundred per core' for uncached Laravel is on the optimistic side; the reference puts 100–300 req/s for the whole 2 vCPU box
grade.notes: Strong, well-reasoned answer: it rejects the rewrite, splits public from per-user endpoints with clear privacy warnings, and covers SWR and purging, load testing, rollback and staffed monitoring. It misses the default throttle and carrier NAT 429 risk, doesn't check Set-Cookie or Authorization headers on public calls, doesn't size MySQL max_connections, and only partly frames costs for the fixed-price contract.
